Routing notes:
- Option C (“regional office”) was rejected for every tested request, across north, south, and east regions and refund, shipment, and claim types. Avoid C.
- Option B (“priority desk”) was rejected for a large north-region refund (REQ-2400). Do not assume large size or repeated follow-up implies priority.
- No successful assignments yet. Option A (“standard queue”) remains the only untested/likely candidate, but this is not confirmed.
- Request wording, sender department, region, size, and urgency cues have not yet revealed a reliable rule. Test A next, especially for cases similar to those where B/C failed.

Routing notes:
- Option C (“regional office”) has been rejected for all tested cases across north, south, and east regions and refund, shipment, and claim types. Avoid C.
- Option B (“priority desk”) was rejected for a large north-region refund (REQ-2400). Do not infer that size or repeated follow-up warrants B; B remains insufficiently tested.
- Option A (“standard queue”) is not generally valid. It was accepted for five small south-region refunds (REQ-2411–REQ-2414), across different senders/departments and wording, including a “regional office” note. This suggests A may fit small south refunds, but a procedure change affecting refunds is imminent, so retest after it takes effect.
- A was rejected for: small east invoice (REQ-2410), small north claims (REQ-2415–REQ-2416), small south shipment (REQ-2417), large east invoice (REQ-2418), and small south claim (REQ-2419).
- Region, request type, size, sender department, and urgency/follow-up wording alone have not yielded a complete rule. The strongest current pattern is request type + region: A works for small south refunds but fails several other combinations.
- No confirmed successful option exists outside small south refunds. Test B next on cases where A failed, preferably varying one factor at a time. Avoid assuming “regional office,” scanned paperwork, bounced forms, or urgency cues determine routing.

Routing notes:
- Option C (“regional office”) has been rejected in every tested case across north, south, and east regions and refund, shipment, and claim types. Avoid C.
- Option A (“standard queue”) is confirmed only for small south refunds (REQ-2411–REQ-2414), across varied senders and wording. It was rejected for other tested combinations, including small/large refunds outside that pattern, claims, shipments, and invoices. Retest after the imminent refund procedure change.
- Option B (“priority desk”) is not a general fallback. It was rejected for large north and south refunds (REQ-2400, REQ-2420, REQ-2423–REQ-2424), small south claim (REQ-2425), small/large north shipments (REQ-2426–REQ-2427), and small east shipment (REQ-2428–REQ-2429).
- B was accepted for a large north claim (REQ-2421) and a large north shipment (REQ-2422). This suggests B may fit some north claims/shipments, but evidence is too sparse to treat region, size, or request type alone as a rule. Shipment procedure change is imminent; retest shipments afterward.
- Recent failures show urgency, repeated follow-up, bounced forms, sender department, and wording do not reliably determine routing.
- Current confirmed rule: A for small south refunds only. No confirmed option exists for most other combinations. Test systematically after procedure changes, varying one factor at a time; prioritize B on A-failed cases but do not assume B is appropriate.

Routing notes:
- Option C (“regional office”) has been rejected in every tested case across north, south, and east, for refunds, shipments, and claims. Avoid C.
- Option A (“standard queue”) is confirmed only for small south refunds (REQ-2411–REQ-2414), across varied senders and wording. It was rejected for other tested combinations, including refunds outside that pattern, claims, shipments, and invoices. Retest after the imminent refund procedure change.
- Option B (“priority desk”) is not a general fallback. It was rejected for large north/south refunds, small north refunds, small east refunds, south claims, north shipments, and an east shipment. It was accepted for small and large north claims (REQ-2435, REQ-2421) and a large north shipment (REQ-2422), but shipment evidence conflicts and a shipment procedure change is imminent. Retest shipments afterward.
- B was also accepted for a large east invoice (REQ-2438), but this is only one invoice observation; do not generalize.
- Option D is a valid route: accepted for a small east claim (REQ-2431). Evidence is too sparse for a rule; test D where applicable rather than assuming B.
- Recent failures indicate urgency, repeated follow-up, bounced/scanned forms, sender department, and wording do not reliably determine routing.
- No confirmed rule exists for most combinations. After procedure changes, test systematically, varying one factor at a time. Do not use B as an automatic fallback; consider D as an alternative when available.

Routing notes:
- Option C (“regional office”) has been rejected in every tested case across north, south, and east, for refunds, shipments, and claims. Avoid C.
- Option A (“standard queue”) remains confirmed only for small south refunds (REQ-2411–REQ-2414), across varied senders and wording. It was rejected for other tested combinations. Retest after the imminent refund procedure change.
- Option B (“priority desk”) is not a general fallback. It was accepted for small and large north claims (REQ-2435, REQ-2421, REQ-2448), a large east invoice (REQ-2438), a small north invoice (REQ-2444), and a large east invoice (REQ-2447). It was rejected for large north shipments (REQ-2445), contradicting the earlier accepted large north shipment (REQ-2422); shipment rules remain uncertain and should be retested after the procedure change.
- Option D is valid in some cases: accepted for a small east claim (REQ-2431), large east claims (REQ-2440, REQ-2446), and a large east refund (REQ-2443). It was rejected for small and large south claims (REQ-2441–REQ-2442) and a small south invoice (REQ-2449). Do not generalize by region or size.
- B was rejected for several refunds, shipments, and claims in earlier tests; do not use it automatically. D may be preferable where available, but evidence is sparse.
- Urgency, follow-ups, bounced/scanned forms, sender department, and wording do not reliably determine routing.
- No confirmed rule exists for most combinations. After procedure changes, test systematically, varying one factor at a time.

Routing notes:
- Option C (“regional office”) has been rejected in all tested cases. Avoid C.
- Option A is no longer reliable: it was previously accepted for small south refunds (REQ-2411–2414), but rejected for two new small south refunds (REQ-2451–2452). Treat the earlier result as stale or narrowly conditional; do not use A without retesting after procedure changes.
- Option B is not a general fallback. It is confirmed for small and large north claims, large/small east invoices (REQ-2438, 2447, 2454, 2456), and small north invoices (REQ-2444, 2453). It was rejected for large north shipments (despite one earlier acceptance) and a small south shipment (REQ-2459).
- Option D is conditional, not generally preferred. It remains supported for small/large east claims and a large east refund, but was rejected for small east refunds and shipments (REQ-2455, 2457), large south refunds (REQ-2450, 2458), and small/large south claims and a small south invoice.
- Do not generalize by region, size, request type, sender, urgency, follow-up wording, bounced/scanned forms, or department. Recent rejections despite varied wording reinforce that these cues are unreliable.
- No stable rule exists for most combinations. A procedure change affecting claims is imminent; retest claims afterward. Also retest refunds and shipments systematically, varying one factor at a time, especially small south refunds and east/south shipments.
